newsitem.title: USA: Badger shareholder seeks to raise stake.
newsitem.headline: Badger shareholder seeks to raise stake.

text.p: A group led by investor James Azzar said it will ask Badger Paper Mills Inc shareholders to allow it to raise its stake to more than 20 percent from the current 14.2 percent.
The group including Bomarko Inc and Extrusions Division Inc disclosed the proxy proposal in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission released on Friday.

The group said it plans to acquire more than 20 percent but less than 50 percent of the total outstanding shares. The proposal will be presented at a special meeting of shareholders on January 23, the filing said.
More shares may be acquired for the purpose of enhancing the group's ability to influence management, to promote a sale of Badger, or to supplement or protect their investment, they said.
Recent actions by Badger and continuing operating losses have cause the group to reevaluate the risks and prospects of its investment, according to the filing.

The group said it intends to communicate with management and take other measures to encourage the board and management to take appropriate measures to maximize stockholders' value, including, if feasible, a sale of Badger or its assets.
The group holds 276,864 common shares or 14.2 percent of the stake with the majority of the shares held by Bomarko. Bomarko is a competitor of Badger in some product lines.
The group said it has no present plans to gain control of the Peshtigo, Wisc., company. Badger is engaged in the manufacture and sale of paper products produced in its integrated systems.
